# Awesome Agents That Learn

**A research guide to self-learning, self-improving, and self-evolving AI agents.**

How do agents turn experience into something useful on the next task? This collection follows the research from reflection and reusable memories to learned skills, agent redesign, self-play, and model updates. Each work explains **what changes, what drives the change, and what evidence supports improvement**.

[Explore the collection](https://duyvuleo.github.io/awesome-agents-that-learn/) · [Start reading](docs/reading-routes.md) · [Browse papers](docs/papers.md) · [Compare benchmarks](docs/benchmarks.md)

**83 annotated works** · 69 papers · 5 surveys · 9 benchmark papers · **8 reading routes**

Source review: **2026-10-28**. 24 entries include inspection of selected full-text sections; 59 are based on primary abstracts/metadata. No linked research code was executed and no published result was independently reproduced for this release.

## Start here

1. Read the [short primer](docs/primer.md) to separate within-task correction from persistent learning.
2. Choose a [reading route](docs/reading-routes.md) and compare mechanisms, rather than reading by date alone.
3. Use the [evaluation guide](docs/evaluation-guide.md) to ask whether gains survive new tasks, a fair baseline, and a fixed budget.
4. Keep your own notes with the [study template](docs/study-template.md).

## A few entry points

These are complementary starting points, not a leaderboard. Their tasks, feedback, and budgets differ.

| Work | Learn this idea |
| --- | --- |
| [Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models](docs/papers.md#voyager) | Builds an expanding library of executable Minecraft skills, retrieved and composed for later tasks. An automatic curriculum proposes objectives, while execution feedback and a model-based critic guide program repair before a skill is retained. |
| [ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners](docs/papers.md#expel) | Collects training-task trajectories, contrasts successes and failures to extract reusable textual insights, and retrieves relevant experiences for new tasks. Learning changes the external experience and insight stores without updating the base model. |
| [DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines](docs/papers.md#dspy) | Represents language-model pipelines as declarative modules and compiles demonstrations for their component prompts. The reusable artifact is an optimized pipeline configuration. |
| [Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents](docs/papers.md#darwin-godel-machine) | A coding agent rewrites its own implementation, and an archive retains runnable variants as possible parents for later edits. This permits exploration beyond the latest or immediately best-performing agent. |
| [Self-Adapting Language Models](docs/papers.md#seal) | Learns to generate synthetic training material or adaptation directives, then applies gradient updates using those edits. An outer reward-based loop improves the edit-generation policy while an inner loop adapts the model. |
| [AgentStream: How Well Do Self-Evolving LLM Agents Perform Under Streaming Tasks?](docs/papers.md#agentstream) | Evaluates retained agent state under isolated domain streams, sequential domain shifts, and interleaved tasks, comparing each evolving agent with a no-evolution baseline. |

## Scope and evidence

The focus is modern language-model-based agents that retain or change a reusable part of their behavior, plus evaluation of that process. We include both externally optimized agent systems and agents that direct their own updates; the annotations explain who or what performs the optimization.

**Core** works directly study persistent agent learning, reusable agent optimization, or its evaluation. **Adjacent** works supply necessary foundations, comparisons, or failure analyses: ordinary tool use, within-task correction, factual memory, and model-only training do not automatically establish a self-evolving agent.

`preprint`, `peer-reviewed`, and `technical-report` describe the inspected publication record, not its scientific quality. Venue notes retain author-reported publication claims when a venue record could not be inspected. `abstract` and `full-text` describe review depth; full-text means selected relevant sections, not exhaustive review. Missing code links mean availability was not verified in this pass. Curator interpretations are marked separately from reported findings.

This is a maintained learning collection with documented coverage limits. It is not an exhaustive survey or a ranking of systems.

## Use and contribute

Search offline with Python 3.10 or newer; no third-party packages are required:

```bash
python3 scripts/explore.py "memory" --scope core
python3 scripts/explore.py --kind benchmark --format json
python3 scripts/explore.py --target agent-code
```

Suggest a paper, correct an annotation, or contribute a reading note through an issue or pull request. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for source requirements and [maintenance](docs/maintenance.md) for validation commands. The canonical records live in [data/papers.json](data/papers.json); generated pages should not be edited directly.

This collection is AI-assisted and maintainer-owned. Automated validation checks structure and consistency; it does not establish scientific truth. No recurring autonomous update job is configured.
